stem: Tariq is developing a client portal for Wareek Accounting in Maryborough. At a weekly meeting, the practice manager wants to see at a glance which tasks are on schedule and which are running late. Which record should Tariq show her?
options: His development journal, with detailed notes from each work session
The Gantt chart, annotated with actual dates and task progress
The test table, with the expected and actual output of every test
The software requirements specification, with the agreed scope
explanation: An annotated Gantt chart shows planned and actual progress side by side for every task, so the manager can see at a glance what is on schedule and what is late. A journal explains why things happened; the chart shows where the whole project stands.
whyWrong: A journal holds detailed notes on causes and decisions, but it doesn't show the whole schedule at a glance.
A test table records test results, not progress against the plan.
The SRS states what the portal must do; it doesn't record progress.

stem: Which activity is part of assessing the effectiveness of a project plan?
options: Comparing planned and actual task durations and explaining the differences
Comparing the solution's actual outputs with the expected outputs in a test table
Comparing users' ratings of the solution with the targets in its evaluation criteria
Comparing the features of the solution with its list of functional requirements
explanation: A project plan is assessed by comparing what was planned with what happened, such as durations and dates, and explaining why they differ.
whyWrong: Comparing actual and expected outputs is testing the solution, not assessing the plan.
Comparing ratings with criteria is part of evaluating the solution, not the project plan.
Checking features against functional requirements judges the solution, not the plan that produced it.

stem: Hargreaves Lane Bakery in Bendigo has had an online ordering app developed. The table compares the planned and actual durations of the project's tasks, which ran one after another. Which conclusion about the project plan is best supported?
options: Testing was poorly planned, because it finished a day early.
The owner's extra screen was the main cause of the delay.
Most of the delay came from a technical issue during coding.
The analysis estimate was the least effective part of the plan.
explanation: The project took 31 days against 25 planned, so it finished 6 days late. Coding alone ran 6 days over because the payment library changed, which is a technical issue. The extra screen added only 1 day, and testing saved 1 day.
whyWrong: Finishing a day early doesn't show poor planning; the estimate was close and offset part of the delay.
The extra screen added only 1 day, while coding ran 6 days over.
Analysis took exactly as long as planned, so its estimate was accurate.

stem: Tawonga Snow Hire's booking system was developed to the plan shown in the Gantt chart, in days. Each task started as soon as the tasks it depended on had finished. The table shows how long each task actually took. How late was the handover compared with the plan?
options: On time
1 day late
5 days late
6 days late
explanation: In the plan, Code booking finishes on day 15, so the handover is on day 19. In fact the booking path took 3 + 5 + 7 = 15 days, but the reports path took 3 + 3 + 10 = 16 days. Test could only start on day 17, after the reports path finished on day 16, so it ran on days 17 to 20 and the handover was on day 20: 1 day late. The reports tasks became the critical path.
whyWrong: The original critical path did finish on time, but the reports path became longer and held up Test.
Code reports ran 5 days over, but its path had 4 days to spare in the plan, so only 1 day passed to the handover.
6 days adds every overrun (1 + 5) as if all the tasks ran one after another.

stem: When Gembrook Lane Legal in Traralgon assessed the project plan for its new client-records program, the journals showed that 9 days had been spent transferring client records from the old system. This task wasn't in the plan. Which improvement to future project plans does this most directly support?
options: Collect more evaluation data after the solution is released
Increase the number of users in the beta testing group
Add more validation checks to the data entry screens
Include data transfer as a task when planning the project
explanation: The delay came from work the plan had left out, so the plan was incomplete. Future plans should list every task, including moving data from an old system, with a realistic duration.
whyWrong: More evaluation data helps judge the solution, not the accuracy of the project plan.
A larger beta test group finds more usability problems but doesn't account for the missing task.
Validation improves the quality of input data but doesn't fix a task missing from the plan.

stem: Carapook Wool Studio in Casterton had an online shop and stock program developed. The tasks ran one after another, and the table compares their planned and actual durations. Which improvement to the next project plan does this evidence most directly support?
options: Add a task for transferring data from the old stock records
Base the coding estimates on this project's actual durations
Keep a second developer available in case a team member leaves
Record and assess each change request before work on it begins
explanation: Both coding tasks took 50% longer than planned, and the journal notes rule out changed requirements and disruptions. That points to unrealistic coding estimates. The actual durations recorded in this project give a better basis for estimating the next one.
whyWrong: Nothing in the evidence shows work that was missing from the plan.
No one left the team; the journal notes rule out a personnel change.
The requirements didn't change, so scope creep didn't cause the overruns.

stem: Dergholm Timber Yard in Edenhope had a sales program developed to the plan shown in the Gantt chart, in days. Every task took exactly its planned duration, yet the handover was 5 days late. The developer's journal for day 8 reads: 'Can't start Code reports. Every report reads the sales tables, and they won't exist until Code database finishes on day 13.' Which conclusion about the project plan is best supported?
options: The time estimate for Code reports was too short
Code database took longer than the plan allowed
A task the reports needed was missing from the plan
The plan left out a dependency between two tasks
explanation: Code reports needed Code database to be finished, but the plan showed it depending only on Design reports. Code reports had to wait until the end of day 13, so it ran on days 14 to 18, Test ran on days 19 to 21, and the handover moved from day 16 to day 21. The durations were right; a dependency was missing.
whyWrong: Every task, including Code reports, took exactly its planned duration.
Code database finished at the end of day 13, as planned.
Code database was in the plan; what was missing was the link from it to Code reports.
